intent_en: Compare how trip shares for car, public transit, biking, and walking differ between transit-oriented developments and the national average, and determine how the two populations compare across all four modes.
narration_support: people who live in these places are less likely than the national average to drive, and more likely to walk, bike, or take transit.
chart_support: Bar chart comparing the share of use for Auto, Public transit, Bike, and Walk between National average and Transit-oriented developments, showing lower Auto reliance and higher reliance on other modes in Transit-oriented developments.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states the behavioral differences (less driving, more walking/biking/transit), and the chart visualizes this by showing lower Auto bars and higher Public transit/Bike/Walk bars for Transit-oriented developments compared to the National average.
narrative_goal: Show that people in transit-oriented developments drive less and use public transit, biking, and walking more than the national average.
intent_machine: To illustrate the transportation behavior differences in transit-oriented developments compared to the national average, specifically highlighting reduced driving and increased use of public transit, biking, and walking.
current_model_input: Compare how trip shares for car, public transit, biking, and walking differ between transit-oriented developments and the national average, and determine how the two populations compare across all four modes.
